scenes.text: Every night it hangs above us, the same face, the same quiet light. This is the story of our Moon.
The Moon is on average about three hundred and eighty four thousand kilometres from Earth.
From new moon to new moon, its phases repeat about every twenty nine and a half days.
It always shows us the same side, because it turns once on its axis for every orbit.
In July 1969, Apollo 11 landed, and twelve people have walked on its surface since.
And during a total lunar eclipse, Earth's shadow turns it a deep red.

props.title: Our Moon
props.subtitle: The light that keeps us company
